response.passage: Electric circuits are pathways that allow electricity to flow continuously. A battery is a collection of two or more cells connected together to provide energy. When a circuit is open, the path is broken, and current cannot flow at all, meaning it does not even reach the switch. Inside our homes, safety is managed by a fuse, which is a wire designed to melt and break the circuit if too much current flows, preventing fires. Contrary to common belief, current is not consumed by a bulb; the same amount of current that enters the bulb leaves it, having only transferred energy. We can also create temporary magnets called electromagnets by wrapping a wire around an iron nail. Increasing the number of turns in this coil strengthens the magnetic field because more current-carrying loops act together. Interestingly, the magnetic effect of current can influence a compass needle even from a distance, without the wire needing to touch it. While electricity and magnetism are related, they are distinct phenomena; magnetism is a force field generated by moving charges, whereas electricity is the flow of those charges themselves.
response.summary: Electric circuits require a complete path to function, with safety devices like fuses protecting against excess current. Electromagnets demonstrate how electricity creates magnetic fields, which are distinct from the electric current itself.
